question.problem:
Find the solutions of $122x≡20\,(\text{mod}\,514).$ Express your answers as nonnegative integers smaller than $514,$ and in ascending order. 

*Hint: You may use the fact that $\text{gcd}(122,514)=2.$*

${x}_{1}≡$
{{field-1}}
$,\,{x}_{2}≡$
{{field-2}}
$\,(\text{mod}\,514)$
question.worked_solution:
In the given congruence, we have $a=122$ and $n=514$, and we're given that

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(122,514)=2.
$$

Since $b=20$ is divisible by $2,$ our congruence has $2$ solutions.

Next, we use the division property of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}122x & ≡20 &  & (\text{mod}\,514) \\ 2\cdot 61x & ≡2\cdot 10 &  & (\text{mod}\,2\cdot 257) \\ \cancel{2}\cdot 61x & ≡\cancel{2}\cdot 10 &  & (\text{mod}\,\cancel{2}\cdot 257) \\ 61x & ≡10 &  & (\text{mod}\,257)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that in this new congruence, we have ${a}_{1}=61$ and ${n}_{1}=257$, where

$$
\text{gcd}({a}_{1},{n}_{1})=\text{gcd}(61,257)=1.
$$

So, our congruence has a unique solution modulo $257.$

To find the solution, we must multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of $61\,(\text{mod}\,257).$ To find the inverse of $61\,(\text{mod}\,257),$ we apply the extended Euclidean algorithm.

First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}257 & = & 61\cdot 4 & + & 13\, & ⇔ & \,13 & = & 257-61\cdot 4 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  &  &  \\ 61 & = & 13\cdot 4 & + & 9\, & ⇔ & \,9 & = & 61-13\cdot 4 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  &  &  \\ 13 & = & 9\cdot 1 & + & 4\, & ⇔ & \,4 & = & 13-9\cdot 1 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  &  &  \\ 9 & = & 4\cdot 2 & + & 1\, & ⇔ & \,1 & = & 9-4\cdot 2 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  &  &  \\ 4 & = & 4\cdot 1 & + & 0\, &  & \, &  & \end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, back-substituting in the usual way gives the following:

$$
1=59\cdot 61-257\cdot 14
$$

We can write this result in modulo $257,$ as follows:  

$$
\begin{aligned}59\cdot 61-257\cdot 14 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,257) \\ 59\cdot 61 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,257)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse of $61$ modulo $257$ is $59.$

Now, multiplying both sides of our original congruence by $59,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}61x & ≡10 &  & (\text{mod}\,257) \\ 59\cdot 61x & ≡59\cdot 10 &  & (\text{mod}\,257) \\ x & ≡590 &  & (\text{mod}\,257) \\ x & ≡257\cdot 2+76 &  & (\text{mod}\,257) \\ x & ≡76 &  & (\text{mod}\,257)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the solution $x≡76\,(\text{mod}\,257).$

But our original congruence was modulo $514$ (not modulo $257$). To find all the solutions modulo $514,$ we repeatedly add $257$ to $76$ modulo $514$ until we reach the number $76$ again:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ≡76 &  & (\text{mod}\,514) \\ {x}_{2} & ≡76+257≡333 &  & (\text{mod}\,514) \\ {x}_{3} & ≡333+257≡590≡514+76≡{x}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,514)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are 

$$
{x}_{1,2}≡76,\,333\,(\text{mod}\,514).
$$
